install_tell: docker run -p 2181:2181 zookeeper:latest (bundled by Kafka/Solr/Druid/Pinot/HBase installs)
misconfig_patterns: Pre-3.5.3 (still common — Kafka bundles ship old ZK): ALL 4lw commands enabled, no whitelist mechanism exists
3.5.3+: 4lw.commands.whitelist defaults to 'srvr' only, but ops guides for Kafka Manager/Burrow/Datadog instruct adding 'mntr,ruok,stat,dump,cons,wchs' — whitelist gets widened back open in practice
AdminServer HTTP interface (default port 8080, distinct from client 2181) exposes /commands/<cmd> as an unauth REST endpoint — same data, different vector, often missed by port-2181-only scanners
wchs/dump commands leak client session IDs and watch paths — session hijack surface
srvr/mntr leak version string for CVE scoping without any auth

active_probe.false_positive_check: raw TCP write of 4-byte command word (no HTTP framing) — response must include 'Zookeeper version:' line; distinguishes from generic TCP echo services on 2181

deployment_tells: raw TCP 'srvr' write to :2181 returns plaintext server stats without auth (4lw)
raw TCP 'mntr' returns Prometheus-style key-value metrics including zk_followers, zk_synced_followers — cluster topology leak
AdminServer REST at :8080/commands/mntr returns same data as JSON, unauth
'dump' 4lw leaks active session list + ephemeral znode owners
pivot_paths: 4LW 'wchs' -> watch paths -> often reveals application znode namespace (e.g. /kafka, /solr, /druid, /helix cluster names)
4LW 'cons' -> connected client IP list -> maps which app servers depend on this ZK ensemble
znode tree walk (if zkCli/native client reachable past the coordination-only 4lw surface) -> full cluster config, ACLs, service registry
vulnerabilities: CVE-2019-8676 (informational disclosure via unrestricted 4lw pre-3.5.3 patch)
CVE-2023-44981 (ZooKeeper SASL quorum auth bypass, unrelated to 4lw but relevant to ensemble compromise chain)
